question: What makes a yo-yo climb back up its string?
answer: The string binds to the spool. When a tug pulls the string from one side of the spool to the other, the yo-yo keeps spinning the same way, so the spool grabs the string and rolls itself back up it. At the bottom of the string the yo-yo is "sleeping": it is still spinning there, waiting for the tug.
move: The spin was there all along; the tug just lets the spool catch the string.
